headline: High: Kestra can ingest and act on outputs from a non-runnable awesome-nlp list, creating default data-flow and compliance risks; prompt injection is limited by the pair's lack of direct shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-nlp is non-runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces, so direct injection into it is impossible. Kestra can read files, stdin/stdout, and many APIs, so if an operator manually copies content from awesome-nlp into a workflow, Kestra could misparse it. The pathway is manual, not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies awesome-nlp content into a Kestra workflow or stdin stream
IF Kestra tasks treat that copied content as instructions or parameters
mitigations: Keep awesome-nlp outputs out of workflow definitions
Use a fixed schema for any copied text
Add a review step before Kestra task execution
Disable ad hoc stdin-based task ingestion where possible

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-nlp touches no data classes and has no egress, but Kestra reads files and can send data to many external services by default. If shared files or workflow inputs contain sensitive material, Kestra can exfiltrate it through HTTP, Slack, email, cloud, or queue integrations. The pair creates a default leakage path through Kestra, not through awesome-nlp.
conditions: IF shared files or workflow inputs contain sensitive data
IF Kestra workflows use any external API, notification, or cloud connector
mitigations: Restrict Kestra connectors to approved destinations
Store sensitive inputs outside shared workflow paths
Mask secrets in logs and notifications
Review workflow inputs before execution
requires-engineering: add DLP or content filtering on Kestra inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot conflict on mutable resources. Kestra can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem, and it supports multiple instances. If both are run in the same workspace, Kestra can overwrite or race on files that awesome-nlp content references, creating a write-conflict risk.
conditions: IF both agents share the same writable directory
IF Kestra workflows modify files that awesome-nlp-derived artifacts reference
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Use read-only mounts for awesome-nlp artifacts
Serialize Kestra jobs touching shared paths
Add file-locking around shared outputs
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-nlp is a curated list, so its outputs can be treated as authoritative recommendations even though they are not executable. Kestra can turn inputs into workflows, notifications, or downstream actions. If a workflow consumes awesome-nlp-derived content without verification, a bad recommendation can cascade into automated actions or alerts.
conditions: IF Kestra uses awesome-nlp-derived text as workflow input or metadata
IF no validation step checks the provenance or correctness of that text
mitigations: Require human approval before execution
Validate inputs against a strict schema
Tag imported content as non-authoritative
Log provenance for every imported item
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action tasks

E_compliance.rationale: awesome-nlp itself touches no regulated data, but Kestra handles logs, inputs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications and can send them to external services. In default orchestration use, that creates a compliance-breach risk if regulated data is routed through Kestra without residency or retention controls. The other agent is not cited because it has no data classes to constrain.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Kestra workflows
IF retention, residency, or notification settings are not explicitly constrained
mitigations: Classify data before it enters Kestra
Disable unnecessary notification channels
Set retention limits on logs and artifacts
Restrict workflows to approved regions
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement
